title: Schedule suggestions recomputation, add retries/backoff, and define staleness behavior
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
We need predictable, low-overhead recomputation of batching/caching suggestions for the Console beta.

This ticket covers:
1) Scheduling policy for the suggestions compute job (cadence + prioritization)
2) Reliability controls (retries, exponential backoff w/ jitter, idempotency)
3) Staleness behavior surfaced to API/UI (so we don’t show ‘fresh’ estimates when the pipeline is lagging)

Scope is specifically the *batching/caching* suggestions pipeline; do not add quantization recommender compute here.

Background/Context
- Console needs stable, conservative estimates and a clear ‘last updated’ signal.
- We’ve already seen telemetry lag / backfill confusion in early dogfood; compute must degrade gracefully.
- Avoid per-request expensive recomputation; compute should run as a batch job driven by aggregated telemetry.

Proposed approach (v0)
A) Scheduling
- Compute job runs on a fixed cadence plus on-demand triggers.
- Cadence:
  - Hourly for orgs/projects that exceed traffic threshold ("active"), to keep estimates reasonably fresh.
  - Daily for low-traffic orgs/projects (reduce cost; avoid noisy estimates).
- “Active” definition (configurable): request_count_1h >= 5k OR token_count_1h >= 50M (numbers are placeholders; finalize with Telemetry + Applied ML).
- Implementation detail: compute is partitioned by (org_id, project_id, route_id, model_id, region) but job orchestration should be per (org_id, project_id) to keep queue sizes sane.

B) Reliability / retries
- Use job queue with at-least-once semantics; compute worker must be idempotent.
- Retry policy:
  - Retry on transient failures (timeouts to aggregates store, network errors, 429/5xx from internal metrics service).
  - Exponential backoff with jitter: 30s, 2m, 8m, 20m (max 4 retries) with random jitter +/- 20%.
  - Do not retry on deterministic input errors (schema mismatch, permission errors, missing required aggregates); mark job failed and emit structured error.
- Concurrency limits:
  - Global worker concurrency cap to avoid stampeding the aggregates store.
  - Per-org cap to avoid one large org starving the queue.

C) Staleness behavior
- Define and implement a consistent staleness rule and surface it in the API response.
- New field(s):
  - stale_as_of: timestamp of the telemetry window end used for the estimate (NOT the compute time).
  - computed_at: timestamp of the compute run.
- Staleness thresholds for beta:
  - Soft stale: stale_as_of older than 24h -> UI shows a “Data may be stale” banner + tooltip.
  - Hard stale: stale_as_of older than 72h -> UI defaults to empty-state variant (“We don’t have recent enough data to make reliable suggestions”) unless the user explicitly toggles “Show stale suggestions”. (UI behavior tracked in DES tickets; backend should provide enough info.)
- When compute is behind (queue lag), we still serve the last computed results but must include stale_as_of and computed_at so the Console can be honest.

D) Observability
- Metrics:
  - suggestions_compute_job_duration_seconds (p50/p95)
  - suggestions_compute_jobs_enqueued_total / succeeded_total / failed_total
  - suggestions_compute_retry_total (by reason)
  - suggestions_compute_queue_lag_seconds
  - suggestions_stale_results_served_total (stale buckets: <24h, 24–72h, >72h)
- Logs:
  - Include org_id, project_id, run_id, attempt, failure_reason, stale_as_of.
- Alerts (owned in ENG-19488 but define signals here):
  - Queue lag > 2h for active cohort
  - Failure rate > 5% over 30m

Acceptance criteria
- A scheduled recompute exists and runs in prod behind the beta feature flag cohort.
- Job retries transient failures with exponential backoff + jitter and does not duplicate/overwrite newer results incorrectly.
- Suggestions API surfaces stale_as_of and computed_at (or equivalent) so Console can explain freshness.
- Clear definition of “soft stale” vs “hard stale” documented in this ticket and in service docs.
- Dashboards can answer: are we behind, who is stale, and why.

Out of scope
- New suggestion types (quantization, routing policy, etc.)
- Automatic application of suggestions.
- Any customer-facing savings guarantees.

comments: 2026-01-24 — Chloe Martin: We’ve had multiple “insufficient telemetry” reports that turned out to be compute lag; please make staleness explicit in the API so Console can message accurately. Also ensure we’re not recomputing everything every hour for low-traffic orgs.

2026-01-28 — Logan Wright: From telemetry side: aggregates for cache hit and latency histograms are finalized with ~15–20m delay in normal operation. Recommend stale_as_of be the *end of the aggregate window* (e.g., last full 5m bucket), not wall-clock compute time.

2026-02-01 — Dr. Maya Srinivasan: For risk/estimates, freshness matters less than stability. Prefer daily recompute for low traffic and only hourly for high confidence cohorts. Please avoid using partial-window aggregates; they can swing savings by 2–3x.

2026-02-04 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): +1 on idempotency. We should treat compute as at-least-once and write results with (org, project, suggestion_id) upsert guarded by computed_at. Also please cap per-org concurrency; one large org can create noisy neighbor issues.

2026-02-08 — Yara Haddad: Drafted scheduling policy: hourly for active, daily for the rest. Implementing job partition per (org, project) with internal fan-out to routes/models. Adding run_id + attempt in logs. Will expose stale_as_of + computed_at fields via suggestions API response object.

2026-02-12 — Nadia Rahman: Please confirm stale thresholds with PM/Design; 72h hard-stale seems reasonable for beta. Also add a metric for “stale served” because we’ll get billing mismatch questions if users see outdated prices/usage assumptions.

2026-02-16 — Yara Haddad: Implementation in PR 22063. Retry policy: 4 retries w/ exponential backoff + jitter; non-retryable errors are schema/validation/missing aggregates. Added per-org concurrency limit = 2 by default (configurable). Wrote results with computed_at monotonic check to avoid overwriting newer run.

2026-02-18 — Dylan Brooks: Reviewed PR; looks good. Please add one more unit test for “late retry attempts don’t clobber newer computed_at” and confirm payload includes stale_as_of even when suggestions list is empty (helps UI empty states).

2026-02-21 — Yara Haddad: Landed. Added clobber-prevention test + ensured API always returns metadata block w/ computed_at/stale_as_of for eligible orgs. Follow-up: tune ‘active cohort’ thresholds after first week of beta using dashboard data (tracked in ENG-19488).
